in_english.name: Uzah
in_english.meaning: Uzah means God's presence, nation, people, surrounding, servant
in_english.long_meaning: Uzah is derived from the Hebrew word Uz, meaning God's presence or the surrounding people. It is a name that signifies spiritual presence, national identity, and servanthood. In the Bible, Uzah is mentioned as a son of Shobal, a son of Reuben (Genesis 46:9). In the Christian tradition, the name Uzah symbolizes devotion, loyalty, and humility. It is a name that encourages its bearers to be mindful of their spiritual presence and their role as servants of God. Uzah is a unique and meaningful name that carries significant weight in Christian culture.

data.cultural_impact: Uzah is mentioned in the Old Testament as a priest of the tribe of Merari who, along with his brother Ahiezer, helped carry the ark of the covenant on a cart during the move from Shiloh to Nob (1 Chronicles 15:13-15 and 2 Samuel 6:1-4). When the oxen stumbled, Uzah reached out and steadied the ark, preventing it from falling, thus preventing a catastrophe from befalling the people. The midrash of the Talmud (Yoma 66b) emphasizes Uzah's heroism and bravery in protecting the ark; he was struck dead immediately afterwards by God because he touched the ark while it was being moved, as God had decreed that it must never be touched except by priests and their descendants.
data.spiritual_significance: Uzah's name symbolizes courage, loyalty, and faith in times of crisis. In the Holy Scriptures, Uzah's story demonstrates how important it is for individuals to remain steadfast and unwavering in their devotion to their faith and their commitment to carrying out the commandments of the Lord, even in the face of hardship and uncertainty. This story continues to inspire the faithful, reminding them of the importance of putting their trust in God and staying steadfast in their faith. It is also a reminder that sometimes, the greatest acts of devotion come in the smallest and seemingly insignificant acts, such as Uzah's intervening to prevent the Ark from falling. Ultimately, the name Uzah serves as a reminder of the power and strength that come from relying upon God and staying faithful to our spiritual principles.
